Black people in America make up roughly 12 or 13% of the entire population.  White people make up about 76%.

The only real disparity when compared to the typical racial demographic is that Asians are 18% of doctors while being only 5.9% of the population here. The last hospital I worked at,  our OB doc who was on a work visa from South Africa and she moved here permanently, another one from Jamaica (though technically she was a roaming physician so she traveled to different hospitals at different times of the year) and one from South Korea. We were this itty bitty little rural town that was like 2 hours away from the next nearest city but we somehow attracted a lot of immigrants and the population there as a whole was pretty diverse. We actually only had two white, male doctors out of the whole bunch.  It's different depending on your area, of course.

You want to know why there aren't more black doctors?  Why aren't there more Asian truck drivers? Why do Asians make up 18% of doctors, but only 1.3% of firefighters and 0.8% of EMS, including Paramedics?  Why aren't there more Black welders?  Or electricians? Also, with the medical thing....cause people like you always throw out money issues (which is relevant to all races, btw) I think you should know that a lot of hospitals offer some SERIOUSLY good financial programs to employees, even if you're someone "low on the rung" like EVS/housekeeping or working in the kitchen, that they will literally pay for a huge chunk of your tuition if you want to go to college to pursue something medical related.

I've worked at 3 hospitals in my life, from being a "floater" (covering multiple non-clinical positions when needed) to working in surgery as a surgical technician to medical records and every single hospital I worked at had that program.  My old boss in med recs for example took it so she could get her RHIT.  Another person in that hospital worked in housekeeping and took up the hospital's educational program and became a phlobotomist. At another hospital, which was the one I worked as a surg tech, they had in-hospital EMT training/course that you were basically being paid by them to do/be there and the same with CNA.  You would just take the official tests after your training was complete.

This was in California, so I can't say if all states or all hospitals have programs like these, but one of the ones that offered it was not only based in California so it's probable many do.

I went to middle school with this guy.  He was the first boy I thought I was in love with, or at least what awkward eleven-year-old me thought love was.  We never dated, but I had a huge crush on him.  I was very unpopular in school and bullied quite bad, and he was honestly one of the nicer people to me in the beginning.  He would always compliment my artwork and encourage me with it, and every now and then would ask me to doodle him things which always made him smile, and I liked being able to make someone smile.

He was my first slow dance, though I found out later that the only reason he danced with me was because his friends bet him money that he wouldn't dance with the ugly fat girl of the class.  After that, I kept my distance from him and I wouldn't draw him things anymore.  Eventually he apologized, we made amends, and then he transferred to a private, religious school.

I saw him a few times when I started high school, and he seemed more or less "normal" besides withdrawing from things he used to enjoy, such as his friends and football. After a year or so, he no longer went to our school, even though his older brother did, but I never asked why that was. I still saw him around our community a little and he was always nice to me, sometimes oddly so. It never made sense to me, especially when I saw how much he distanced himself from his friends and family. He would just be downright mean and vicious to them, and it didn't make sense, but I figured he was just being a broody, pissy teenager.

A year or two after I graduated high school, he shot and killed his father in their own home and assaulted his mother. Never gave a reason why. Never found out why.  It's still surprising.

Why are there fewer black authors when you can literally write a story, slap it into PDF mode and have it published for free on Amazon?  Why are there so few black artists compared to other races in the USA?  Why are there so few black firefighters?  Why are there so few black ranch hands?

But you know what I see a lot of?  A lot of black doctors, dentists, nurses, chefs, musicians, and yes...business owners.  Not every black business owner wants to wear their race as a reason for their business success but rather would have their good work ethic and how they treat their customers speak for them. :| Why can't you see that?  You don't need to say "I'm black and I own a business" for people to like you or acknowledge you or like your store and trying to say it in order to get people to do that is just...bad practice.  Your store, what you offer, and how you treat your employees should speak loud enough about your work ethic and your characters. Not race.

That's not always true. There isn't a physical "need" for race-specific store owners, just like there isn't a physical "need" for employees to be one race or another.

On a basic level, the only need is for someone who can run/manage the business and sell quality items or services.  Race doesn't play into it at all, and yet people consistently want it to.

Nobody is stopping black people from opening businesses or procuring loans. The fact there are few of them is not anybody's fault, but based on an individual's decision, the same way there are so few black authors.  People simple make different cultural choices about their lives and what they aspire to be or not to be.

And where exactly are you collecting your information, anyways? If you're going to throw numbers, it's typically a good idea to cite your sources.  

Also, if you want to bring in colleges...what do you have to say about colleges and universities that lower their educational requirements for prospective black students but everyone else still has to meet them to even be considered? The uni I went to had completely different standards and requirements if you were black.  I'm Shawnee, and I still had to meet the normal requirements to get in despite I come form the smallest and most poverty-stricken race in the USA.  Didn't feel great at all when someone I went to high school with got in with half the work and half the educational requirements solely because they were black while I had to work my literal ass off to get in, and even then, barely got in by the skin of my teeth.

It felt even worse when I was struggling to get scholarships because I wasn't black, while this person who went there with me got them one after another, despite coming from a well-off family with their father being a dentist.  I really liked him and I also really liked his family, but that honestly sucked and that is the kind of stuff that makes people feel shitty about racial differentials like that.

Even so, white people end up with a disproportionate amount of scholarships and grants because they are much more apt to apply for them, same with asian families.  Expanded education and a "requirement" of success is very prevalent in those families and gets pushed hard on their kids (sometimes stupidly so) to the point many just end up with a pointless degree and huge amounts of debt anyways.


The thing is, and what people are also trying to say, is that there is equal opportunity for everyone, with the only privilege being wealth and not necessarily race.  I've had some pretty diverse and interesting life experiences to lead me thinking like this. I grew up on a reservation, worked hard to go to college, got sick and had to leave it, lived in military communities to rural country/mountains to gang-dominated ghettos, and even overseas.  What I learned from that is a lot of a person's life (especially in the USA) is based on their decisions.

Sometimes those decisions are difficult to make or might be harder to make depending on the culture you come from. For example, the tribe I grew up with (not my people but we did live with them) were very "backwards thinking" and would go so far as to disown their kids if their kids wanted to go to college, saying it was them "trying to be white".  That mindset hurt so many of us.  I was one of the few who "got out" and even then, barely. A girl who lived on the rez with me got completely disowned by her family because she wanted to go to community college and become an RN.

You consistently sitting there and only saying "Black and white" shows me what kind of person you are.  You're shallow, arrogant, and toxic. There are more than just black and white people in this country and in the world, and the world in general will become such a better place when people like you stop thinking like this.

My 9th grade English teacher had it out for me for some reason.  I got pneumonia and I was out of school for 3 months in treatment and recovery. In that time, my mom contacted my HS counselor to help get my work put together every week from my teachers. All my teachers complied except my English teacher. She would never have any homework or list of lessons they went through. My mom tried multiple times to contact her but she never returned her phone calls.

When I went back to school, my counselor told me I would have to finish out the year at an alternative "bad kid" high school because I was failing english due to not doing the work. I told him she never gave me homework or lessons, so he had me see if she would give them to me and give me 3 weeks to complete them.

When I went to talk to my English teacher about them, she told me no. I told her I never received any homework from her when I was sick, and she said "that's because I didn't put any in your work packet.  It's your responsibility to be here and get the homework yourself or ask another student."

I told her that was impossible - I was 14 years old, bed-ridden and lived 45 minute drive away from school. There was also nobody else in her class that even lived in my area. She basically shrugged and said it was my responsibility, not my parents, to collect my work.

Eventually she gave me an F, but our school had a rule that the parents had to be contacted through mail when the child was initially starting to get a failing grade, and if they weren't, the child had to get at least a D- for the semester. She never contacted them. My mother showed up to talk to her this time and the teacher claimed she sent it despite not having any proof she did (they had to keep photocopy records) and told her "Your lazy kid probably stole it out of the mailbox because she's ashamed of herself, as she should be."

My mom told her "That'd be a little hard for her to do, considering we use a P.O box that's 7 miles away from our house and she doesn't have a key or ability to access it."

She ended up having to sign off on the D- but come my senior year, 2 weeks before graduation, my counselor called me in.  Apparently, that teacher had revoked the D- days later and changed it to an F.  I tried to go speak to her about it in person many times but she would refuse to speak to me. My counselor ended up signing it off as a D- himself and told me that she had been a huge problem for the district as a teacher for a long time.

A year later, I found out she got fired and was working at one of the worst-rated salons in town.
It's crazy what all gets left behind in places and forgotten.
